name: Ferrari 512S Coda Lunga
description:
The Ferrari 512S Coda Lunga ("long tail") is a streamlined variant of the 512 S developed specifically for the high-speed straights of Le Mans. In the ongoing battle against the dominant Porsche 917, Ferrari's engineers sought every possible aerodynamic advantage for the 1970 24 Hours of Le Mans.

The Coda Lunga featured an extended, tapered rear bodywork designed to reduce drag on the Mulsanne Straight, where cars reached their maximum velocities. This long-tail configuration sacrificed some downforce for reduced air resistance, a worthwhile trade-off on a circuit where top speed was crucial to competitive lap times.

Beneath the sleek bodywork sat the same formidable 4,993cc V12 engine as the standard 512 S, producing approximately 560 horsepower at 8,500 RPM. The all-aluminum powerplant with four valves per cylinder was developed under the direction of Mauro Forghieri as Ferrari's answer to the new 5-liter Group 5 regulations.

The 1970 Le Mans saw an epic battle between Ferrari and Porsche, with the 512S Coda Lunga variants reaching speeds over 320 km/h on the Mulsanne. Although Porsche ultimately prevailed that year, the long-tail 512 S remains one of the most beautiful and purposeful racing cars ever created, its flowing lines representing the pinnacle of late-1960s aerodynamic thinking applied to endurance racing.
